title: GCSE English Literature
intro: Macbeth, Scrooge, the Birlings and more: test your knowledge of the set texts and the poetry terms examiners love.

questions.prompt: In Macbeth, which character discovers King Duncan's body?
questions.explanation: Macduff arrives early at the castle to wake the king and is the first to find that Duncan has been murdered.

questions.prompt: Which character in Macbeth says "Out, damned spot!" while sleepwalking?
questions.explanation: Lady Macbeth tries to rub away a spot of blood only she can see, showing how guilt has broken her mind.

questions.prompt: Which new title do the witches promise Macbeth that he is given almost straight away?
questions.explanation: The witches hail Macbeth as Thane of Cawdor, and soon afterwards Ross tells him King Duncan has given him that title.

questions.prompt: What do the witches predict for Banquo's descendants?

options.label: They will be thanes of Glamis

questions.explanation: The witches say Banquo will father kings without being king himself, which makes Macbeth fear and resent him.

questions.prompt: King James I, on the throne when Macbeth was first performed, had written a book about which subject?
questions.explanation: James I wrote Daemonologie about witchcraft, so the witches in Macbeth would have fascinated his court.

questions.prompt: In A Christmas Carol, who is the first ghost to visit Scrooge?

options.label: The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come

questions.explanation: Scrooge's dead business partner, Jacob Marley, appears in chains to warn him to change his ways.

questions.prompt: What is the name of Bob Cratchit's youngest son, who is unwell?
questions.explanation: Tiny Tim's illness and kindness move Scrooge and help show the hardship faced by poor families.

questions.prompt: Which two children does the Ghost of Christmas Present reveal beneath his robe?
questions.explanation: The boy is Ignorance and the girl is Want. Dickens uses them to warn readers about neglecting the poor.

questions.prompt: Dickens divided A Christmas Carol into five sections. What did he call them?
questions.explanation: A stave is a verse of a song, which fits the idea of the book being a 'carol'.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the Inspector in An Inspector Calls?
questions.explanation: His name, Goole, sounds like 'ghoul', a hint that he may not be an ordinary police officer.

questions.prompt: Who wrote An Inspector Calls?
questions.explanation: J. B. Priestley wrote the play to make audiences think about social responsibility.

questions.prompt: In An Inspector Calls, which member of the Birling family is engaged to Gerald Croft?
questions.explanation: The play opens with the Birlings celebrating Sheila's engagement to Gerald Croft.

questions.prompt: Mr Birling confidently tells his guests which ship is 'unsinkable'?
questions.explanation: The audience knows the Titanic sank in 1912, so Priestley uses dramatic irony to show Mr Birling is not as wise as he thinks.

questions.prompt: What name does the Inspector first give for the young woman at the centre of his investigation?
questions.explanation: The Inspector speaks of Eva Smith, who also used the name Daisy Renton later in the play.

questions.prompt: In Romeo and Juliet, which family does Juliet belong to?
questions.explanation: Juliet is a Capulet and Romeo is a Montague, two families locked in a long feud.

questions.prompt: Which of Romeo's friends cries "A plague o' both your houses!"?
questions.explanation: Mercutio blames both feuding families for his fate, a key turning point in the play.

questions.prompt: Who secretly marries Romeo and Juliet?
questions.explanation: Friar Laurence agrees to marry them, hoping the match will end the feud between their families.

questions.prompt: Who wrote Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde?
questions.explanation: Robert Louis Stevenson published the novella in 1886.

questions.prompt: Which lawyer and friend of Dr Jekyll investigates the mystery of Mr Hyde?
questions.explanation: Gabriel Utterson, Jekyll's lawyer, follows most of the story and tries to uncover who Hyde is.

questions.prompt: In which city is Jekyll and Hyde mainly set?
questions.explanation: The story takes place in Victorian London, with its foggy streets and contrast between respectable and poorer areas.

questions.prompt: When a sentence runs on from one line of poetry into the next without a pause, this is called…
questions.explanation: Enjambment carries the meaning over the line break and can create pace or surprise.

questions.prompt: What is a pause in the middle of a line of poetry, often marked by punctuation, called?
questions.explanation: A caesura breaks up the rhythm of a line and can make the reader stop and think.

questions.prompt: Unrhymed lines of iambic pentameter, as used in much of Shakespeare's writing, are called…
questions.explanation: Blank verse has a regular rhythm but no rhyme. Shakespeare's noble characters often speak in it.

questions.prompt: In Macbeth, Banquo becomes king after Duncan's death.
questions.explanation: It is Macbeth who is crowned. Banquo never becomes king, though the witches say his descendants will.

questions.prompt: In An Inspector Calls, Gerald Croft is Mr Birling's son.
questions.explanation: Eric is Mr Birling's son. Gerald Croft is Sheila's fiancé and the son of a rival business family.

questions.prompt: At the start of Romeo and Juliet, Juliet is not yet 14 years old.
questions.explanation: Her mother and the Nurse both say Juliet will turn 14 in about two weeks.

questions.prompt: A dramatic monologue is a poem spoken by a single character, often to a listener who does not reply.
questions.explanation: In a dramatic monologue one voice speaks, revealing their character through what they say.

questions.prompt: In which year is An Inspector Calls set?
questions.explanation: The play is set in spring 1912, just before the Titanic sails and two years before the First World War.

questions.prompt: In which year was A Christmas Carol first published?
questions.explanation: Dickens published A Christmas Carol in December 1843, at a time of great poverty in Victorian Britain.

questions.prompt: How many syllables does a regular line of iambic pentameter have?
questions.explanation: Iambic pentameter has five iambs, each an unstressed then a stressed syllable, making ten syllables.
